summary: Nobuo Otsuka specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University from circa 1983 to 1988 and served as a researcher there, attested in 1995.

Nobuyoshi Yamabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Otani, Osaka, and Yale universities. He held positions at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, Tokyo University of Agriculture, and Waseda University.

Nobuyuki Kaji is a scholar of Sinology and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University. He taught at Koshien Junior College, Nagoya University, Osaka University, Koyasan University, Doshisha University, and Ritsumeikan University.

Nobuyuki Watase is an Indologist who completed his master's studies at Kyoto University around 1966–1969. He served as an associate professor (circa 1977–1985) and professor (circa 1985–2012) at Tokai University.

Nobuyuki Yoshimoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and Genjun Sasaki. He held positions at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science and Otani University.

Norbert M. Samuelson was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Northwestern, Hebrew Union College, and Indiana University, and held a post at Arizona State University from circa 1998 to 2020.

Noriaki Hakamaya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He taught primarily at Komazawa University and Komazawa Junior College, and visited the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
Noriaki Hosoda works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held posts as an assistant (attested 1986) and associate professor (attested 2003) at Hokkaido University.
Noriaki Inoue is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from circa 1949 to 1953. He later served as a professor at Taisho University from circa 1975 to 1999.
Norihiko Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Osaka Kyoiku University from circa 1964 to 1968. He served as a professor at Bukkyo University from circa 1995 to 2015.
Norihiko Uchida specializes in linguistics and Indology and studied under Yutaka Ochihara. In 1962, he held posts at the Osaka University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo.
Norihisa Baba is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo, where he later held posts at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.
Norio Koyama is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami. He became a professor at Taisho University circa 2008.

Noritoshi Aramaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied at Kyoto University. He held professorships at Kyoto University, Osaka University, and Otani University, among other appointments.

Noriyuki Kudo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed postgraduate studies at Bukkyo University. He held positions at Bukkyo University, Soka University, and the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology.
Norvin Hein was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Franklin Edgerton. He served as an associate professor of comparative religion at Yale Divinity School, attested in 1965.

Nosei Fuji is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University. Fuji held posts at Daegu University, Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, the Buddhist Cultural Institute, the Institute for Religious Culture, and Ryukoku University.

Notto R. Thelle is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He was associate director of the NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions in 1974 and held a post at the University of Oslo (~1986–2006).

Noémie Verdon is a scholar of Indology and archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Lausanne under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand, and held a post at Kyoto University attested in 2019.
Nyanaponika Thera was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Ceylon. He served as an editor at the Buddhist Publication Society from circa 1958 to 1984.
